definitions.gloss: to drive into, to chase into
definitions.explanation: To force someone or something into a confined space by chasing.

definitions.gloss: to corner, to push into a difficult situation
definitions.explanation: To force someone into a desperate or disadvantageous position, either literally or figuratively.

examples.japanese: {羊|ひつじ}を{囲|かこ}いに{追|お}い{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To drive the sheep into the pen.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}がネズミを{部屋|へや}の{隅|すみ}に{追|お}い{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: The cat chased the mouse into a corner of the room.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}を{袋小路|ふくろこうじ}に{追|お}い{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: The criminal was cornered in a dead end.

examples.japanese: {借金|しゃっきん}で{彼|かれ}は{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた{状況|じょうきょう}にある。
examples.english: He's in a desperate situation due to debt.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}を{追|お}い{込|こ}んでトレーニングする。
examples.english: To push oneself hard during training.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB: {追|お}う (to chase) + {込|こ}む (to go into) = to chase into

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive. Takes を to mark what is being driven/cornered.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{窮地|きゅうち}に{追|お}い{込|こ}む (to drive into a tight spot)
・{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる (to be cornered - passive form)
・{自分|じぶん}を{追|お}い{込|こ}む (to push oneself)
・{崖|がけ}っぷちに{追|お}い{込|こ}む (to push to the brink)

USAGE NOTE: Often used in the passive form {追|お}い{込|こ}まれる when describing being put in a difficult situation.

RELATED ～{込|こ}む COMPOUND VERBS:
・{呼|よ}び{込|こ}む - to call in, to invite in
・{誘|さそ}い{込|こ}む - to lure into
・{駆|か}け{込|こ}む - to rush into
